name: Calendly
tagline: Scheduling links for booking meetings without back-and-forth email

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Standard listed at $12/seat/month monthly and $10/seat/month annually.
pricing.freeTier: The free plan covers one event type on one connected calendar.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 1 one-on-one event type, 1 connected calendar and unlimited scheduled meetings.

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.limits: Unlimited event types; connect up to 6 calendars; 1 seat per paid user.

tiers.name: Teams
tiers.limits: Unlimited event types; up to 6 connected calendars; round-robin and routing.
tiers.notes: Annual price falls incrementally by seat band: $16 for seats 1–30, then $14.50 for 31–50, $14 for 51–100, $13.50 for 101–200, $13 for 201–300 and $12 for 301+.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Starts at a $15,000 annual contract; numeric user and event limits are custom.
tiers.notes: Starting annual contract divided by 12; invoicing and enterprise terms are custom.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 one-on-one event type, 1 connected calendar and unlimited meetings.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; 14-day paid-plan trial falls back to Free; Enterprise starts at $15,000/year
pricing.hiddenCosts: Every owner and admin occupies a paid seat; newly added seats are prorated and all users in one organization must share a plan. SAML SSO is a paid add-on with no public price.

verdictSummary: A single-user booking page is easy; production-grade scheduling needs OAuth, availability rules, time zones, reminders, payments, team routing, and trust.
coreLoopDIY: Connect calendar, publish event-type pages, let guests choose available slots, create calendar events, and send reminders.
whatYouLose: polished Google/Outlook OAuth kept working for you
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because double-booking or missed meeting invites is costly.

priorArt.name: cal.com
priorArt.desc: open-source Calendly; self-host and skip the OAuth pain

alternatives.name: Cal.com Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited solo event types, calendars and bookings, with payments and notifications; team routing costs money.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose with PostgreSQL for self-hosting
facts.dataFormat: Hosted bookings, availability, integrations, and attendee data live in Cal.com's cloud; self-hosted deployments store core data in PostgreSQL and files or integration data in the configured services.
facts.gapVsPaid: Cal.com's broader, more technical product is less turnkey, and team routing, collective scheduling, and organization controls remain paid.
facts.setupBlocker: The hosted product is straightforward, but self-hosting requires Docker, PostgreSQL, environment secrets, email delivery, OAuth credentials, a domain, and upgrades.

alternatives.name: Google Calendar appointment schedules
alternatives.desc: One bare appointment page inside the calendar you already use; reminders, payments and polish are paid.

facts.install: Use the appointment-schedule feature inside Google Calendar
facts.dataFormat: Availability and bookings are stored as Google Calendar and appointment-schedule data in the user's Google account; the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: A personal Google account gets only one booking page and lacks Calendly's paid reminders, payment collection, screening forms, and automation integrations.

alternatives.name: Koalendar Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited booking pages and two calendar connections; payments, forms, reminders and team routing are paid.

facts.dataFormat: Booking pages, invitee answers, and availability settings live in Koalendar's cloud, while confirmed bookings are synchronized to connected Google, Outlook, or iCloud calendars; the internal format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: Payments, intake forms, automated reminders, group events, and team routing are paid, so the free product stops at uncomplicated one-to-one scheduling.
facts.setupBlocker: The first setup step is granting calendar OAuth access; paid-only forms, reminders, payments, and team features appear quickly once the booking flow becomes more than basic.

alternatives.name: TidyCal Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited one-person booking types and paid bookings on one calendar; group meetings and fancy emails cost extra.

facts.install: Hosted signup and one calendar connection
facts.dataFormat: Booking types, attendee answers, and booking records live in TidyCal's cloud and are synchronized to the connected calendar; the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: The free plan connects only one calendar and withholds group meetings, custom emails, automatic video links, and analytics.
facts.setupBlocker: Connecting the calendar is easy, but the free account is limited to one calendar and omits several workflow customizations.

alternatives.name: YouCanBookMe Free
alternatives.desc: One booking page, but it keeps forms, payments, confirmations, polls and the calendar-overlay trick.

facts.install: Hosted signup and one calendar connection
facts.dataFormat: Booking-page configuration and appointment records live in YouCanBookMe's cloud, with events synchronized to the connected calendar; the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: The free account is limited to one booking page and one connected calendar, so separate meeting types or calendars quickly force an upgrade.
facts.setupBlocker: The setup itself is clean; the obstacle is structural rather than technical, one booking page and one connected calendar.

alternatives.name: zcal Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited links and calendars, custom questions, email reminders and Stripe payments; teams are paid and zcal takes 3%.

facts.dataFormat: Scheduling links, availability, answers, and booking records live in zcal's cloud and synchronize to connected calendars; the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: Team and routing features are paid, and free-plan Stripe payments lose an additional 3% to zcal.
facts.setupBlocker: Calendar OAuth is straightforward, but accepting Stripe payments on the free plan adds zcal's 3% commission.

alternatives.name: Zoho Bookings Free
alternatives.desc: A real one-person booking desk with forms, reminders and two-way sync; staff and payment plumbing cost extra.

facts.dataFormat: Services, availability, customer details, and bookings live in Zoho's cloud and synchronize with connected calendars; the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: The free plan is limited to one user and leaves payment integrations, team scheduling, and advanced workflow customization to paid tiers.
facts.setupBlocker: A Zoho account and calendar connection are easy; configuring services, time zones, and notification rules is the first non-trivial step.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Cal.diy
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Self-hostable, yes; also explicitly a hobbyist, non-production fork that expects database and security expertise.

notes: The booking page is easy. Calendar-sync OAuth is where weekends go to die; be honest with yourself about that before starting.
prompt:
Build me a personal booking page like Calendly. Requirements:

- A public /book page showing my available slots for the next 14 days; visitors
  pick one, enter name + email + note, and get a confirmation page.
- Availability = weekly rules in a config file (e.g. Mon–Fri 10:00–17:00,
  30-min slots, 15-min buffer between meetings, my timezone) minus existing
  bookings, rendered in the visitor's local timezone.
- Google Calendar sync via OAuth (credentials in .env): busy events block slots,
  and confirmed bookings are created in my calendar with the visitor invited and
  a Google Meet link attached. Warn me in the README: this OAuth app setup is
  the fiddly part · budget an hour for the Google Cloud console alone.
- Email confirmations to both sides via SMTP creds in .env.
- Cancel/reschedule links with a signed token in the email.
- SQLite storage, one Node process, no accounts, no framework lock-in.
